mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST and GDPC1 over a 6-month window indicates robust housing demand coinciding with overall demand growth, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the 6-month correlation between HOUST and GDPC1 exceeds 0.7.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in RSAFS below its 5-year minimum indicates a severe contraction in retail sales, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls below its 5-year minimum on a year-over-year basis.
